html:
SMTO-SSH-0002 — SMTO couldn't use the saved details for this SSH connection

GUID: f2d9ea5d-df80-453f-bfdc-be5d42cbcb20
Slug: ssh-target-invalid
Domain: SSH · Subsystem: ssh

What happened

  • SMTO remembers which computer, account and port each SSH command used. One of those saved details is missing or in a form SMTO can't use, so it couldn't reuse them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the computer name, user name and port in the SSH command you asked SMTO to run. Names can use only letters, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores and colons, and the port must be 1 to 65535. SMTO can only save connection details in that form, so other characters or ports leave the saved details unusable.
  2. Start a new conversation by typing /new and ask SMTO to run the SSH command there. The unusable details are saved with this conversation; a new one saves fresh details after its first successful connection.
  3. If the same message appears in the new conversation, select Copy error details in this panel. Details SMTO has just saved from a working connection should always be usable, so a repeat needs someone to look into it.

What success looks like

  • The SSH command runs and its output appears, and later SSH commands to the same computer work in that conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the exact SSH command you asked for, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep repeating the same command unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SSH setup validation rejected a remembered target: missing fields or Gateway identity, an alias, host or user outside the allowed character set, a port outside 1–65535, or a config reference longer than 512 characters or containing control characters.

What this means

  • Public SSH setup validation rejects its required fields, target names, integer port or bounded configuration reference; the Controller adapter also requires a Gateway. Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.

Why this can happen

  • Public SSH setup validation rejects its required fields, target names, integer port or bounded configuration reference; the Controller adapter also requires a Gateway.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the selected Gateway and exact rejected alias/host/user/port/config_ref field.

How to fix it

  • validate_public in src/gateway_core/ssh_context.py requires exactly the public fields, alias/host/user matching [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.:%-]* (at most 253 characters), an integer port 1–65535 and a config_ref of at most 512 printable characters; the SSH resource adapter also requires a Gateway identity. Correct the target in the requested ssh command and re-enroll it from a successful verified connection.
  • Correct the intended host/user and port (1–65535), then use the exact public configuration reference returned by supported discovery.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported discovery returns a complete public setup for the intended SSH target.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
